rows.text: The PMO release reports that on 25 January 2006 the Supreme Court jury convicted Hon. Veikune (Siosifa Fatafehi Fuatakifolaha Veikune) and that under Clause 23 of the Constitution he is deemed to be no longer an elected representative; it states that on 3rd February 2006 the Acting Private Secretary to His Majesty confirmed that 'his position as the Speaker of the House ended on 25th January, 2006'.
rows.uncertainty: The end day is stated, as confirmed on behalf of the Palace on 3 February 2006 (separate claim), in a government release, not in the Palace letter itself. The conviction is context; the end rests on the stated day, not on the conviction.

rows.text: The same release states: 'Last Friday, 3rd February 2006, the Acting Private Secretary to His Majesty, Mr. Sateki 'Ahio, thanked Fuatakifolaha Veikune, and confirmed that his position as the Speaker of the House ended on 25th January, 2006.'
rows.uncertainty: 'Last Friday' is resolved by the release itself, which prints the date. The confirming letter is not reproduced.

rows.text: The release, dated 'Feb 9, 2006, 12:20', states that 'A new Speaker of the House is expected to be appointed soon', to be followed by a by-election for the Nobles of Vava'u to fill their vacant seat in the House.
rows.uncertainty: The release does not say that the Speakership is vacant: its 'vacant seat' is the Vava'u nobles' seat. That no Speaker was then in office is implied by the expected appointment, not stated, and no acting Speaker is named. The successor's appointment is not in this source.
